section: Land revenue systems - Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari and Mahalwari; areas and effects
subsections: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro

accepted.s: The first experimental introduction of the Ryotwari system in the Madras Presidency took place in which area?
accepted.x: The first experiment was conducted in Baramahal, comprising areas such as Salem, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri and Tiruvannamalai.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first experimental area from the later area of wider implementation.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Baramahal came under the control of the East India Company as a consequence of which event?
accepted.x: Baramahal came to the Company after the Third Mysore War in 1792.
accepted.tq: Link a territorial acquisition with the correct war rather than with a similar treaty or conflict.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who conducted the first experiment of the Ryotwari system in Baramahal?
o: R.M. Bird, assisted by James Thomason
Captain Alexander Read, assisted by Thomas Munro
Thomas Munro, assisted by Holt Mackenzie
accepted.x: Captain Alexander Read introduced the experiment in Baramahal with Thomas Munro as his assistant.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–assistant relationship to avoid swapping officials associated with different settlements.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Thomas Munro's headquarters as the first Collector of the Ceded Districts was located at:
accepted.x: Munro's headquarters as the first Collector of the Ceded Districts was at Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Separate an official headquarters from the place of death and the wider regional headquarters.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Thomas Munro died of cholera at which place in 1827?
accepted.x: Thomas Munro died of cholera at Pattikonda in present-day Kurnool district in 1827.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a person's administrative headquarters and place of death.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following best explains Thomas Munro's preference for a direct settlement with the peasant?
o: He wished to strengthen the authority of the Palegars.
He wanted revenue to depend exclusively on crop prices.
He distrusted Palegars and large intermediaries.
He intended to abolish all village officers.
accepted.x: Munro distrusted Palegars and big intermediaries and therefore favoured settling revenue directly with the cultivator.
accepted.tq: Infer the administrative choice from the official's stated preference and distrust of intermediaries.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which linguistic ability of Thomas Munro facilitated his work in the Madras territories?
o: He spoke Telugu fluently and worked without interpreters.
He spoke Kannada fluently and worked through Palegars.
He spoke Tamil fluently and worked without village officers.
He spoke Persian fluently and worked through zamindars.
accepted.x: Munro spoke Telugu fluently and was able to work without interpreters.
accepted.tq: Test a distinctive personal detail against nearby language and intermediary traps.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Ceded Districts, the Ryotwari system was extended by Thomas Munro in 1802 after he had:
accepted.x: Munro introduced Ryotwari in the Ceded Districts in 1802 after suppressing the Palegars.
accepted.tq: Connect an administrative reform with the immediate regional political development.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why was the Ryotwari system considered suitable for the Ceded Districts?
o: The region had no strong zamindars, and Munro opposed strengthening the Palegars.
The region had already adopted the Mahalwari system.
The region was entirely under urban merchant control.
The region had powerful zamindars who could guarantee collection.
accepted.x: Munro considered the system suitable because the Ceded Districts lacked strong zamindars and he did not want to strengthen the Palegars.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the regional condition with the administrator's policy objective.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the geographical distribution of revenue systems in the Madras Presidency is correct?
o: Haveli lands were permanently settled with zamindars before British control.
The Northern Circars were entirely under Ryotwari from the beginning.
The Northern Circars were mainly under zamindari settlement, while Haveli lands later came under Ryotwari.
The Ceded Districts were mainly governed through the Mahalwari system.
accepted.x: The Northern Circars were mainly zamindari areas, whereas Haveli lands under direct British control later came under Ryotwari.
accepted.tq: Compare neighbouring regional arrangements and identify the qualified statement.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Ryotwari system, which of the following rights was available to the ryot so long as the assessment was paid?
o: Only the right to cultivate, without transfer rights
The right to sell, mortgage, gift or lease the land
The right to remit all land revenue permanently
The right to collect revenue from other cultivators
accepted.x: The ryot held proprietary rights and could sell, mortgage, gift or lease the land as long as the assessment was paid.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal incidents of ryot ownership rather than confusing them with revenue-collection powers.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Ryotwari settlement:
1. Settlement was made ryot by ryot.
2. Revenue was fixed on the land rather than directly on the crop produced.
3. The assessment was ordinarily revised about every thirty years.
4. Karanams and village officers worked under the Collector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements describe features of the Ryotwari arrangement: individual settlement, land-based assessment, periodic revision and supervision through village officers under the Collector.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of features while checking whether the option preserves the full set.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Ryotwari system, the amount of revenue could rise or fall primarily with changes in:
o: the number of zamindars in the district
the market value of urban property
accepted.x: Ryotwari revenue was linked to the actual area cultivated, so the amount could rise or fall accordingly.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the determining factor in Ryotwari from unrelated administrative and market factors.
accepted.sec: Ryotwari - first area in Madras Presidency, Read and Munro  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the Lists:

List-I (Official)
a. Holt Mackenzie
b. R.M. Bird
c. James Thomason

a. List-II (Role)
i. Carried on Bird's settlement in the NWP
ii. Devised the Mahalwari system
iii. Revised the system through a survey-based settlement

The correct matching is:
accepted.x: Holt Mackenzie devised the system, R.M. Bird revised it through survey-based settlement, and James Thomason carried on Bird's settlement in the NWP.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure official–role pair and eliminate codes that repeat the wrong function.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Regulation VII of 1822 is associated with the work of which official in relation to the Mahalwari system?
accepted.x: Holt Mackenzie devised the Mahalwari system under Regulation VII of 1822.
accepted.tq: Match the regulation number with the official who formulated the arrangement.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: R.M. Bird is remembered in connection with the Mahalwari system mainly because he:
o: revised the system through a survey-based settlement under Regulation IX of 1833
created the zamindari system in Bengal
accepted.x: R.M. Bird revised the Mahalwari system through a survey-based settlement under Regulation IX of 1833 during Bentinck's period.
accepted.tq: Use the official's specific reform role to distinguish him from the original designer and later executor.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: R.M. Bird is described as the 'father of land settlement in north India' because of his association with:
o: the suppression of Palegars in Rayalaseema
the survey-based revision of the Mahalwari settlement
the direct settlement with ryots in Madras
the permanent fixation of zamindari revenue in Bengal
accepted.x: Bird's major contribution was the survey-based revision of the Mahalwari settlement in north India.
accepted.tq: Link an epithet with the particular administrative contribution that earned it.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: James Thomason's role in the Mahalwari settlement was to:
o: carry on R.M. Bird's settlement in the North-Western Provinces as Lieutenant-Governor
introduce the system in the Ceded Districts
enforce the Permanent Settlement in Bengal
accepted.x: James Thomason carried on Bird's settlement in the North-Western Provinces while serving as Lieutenant-Governor.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later executor of a settlement from its original designer and reviser.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of British India was covered by the Mahalwari system?
accepted.x: The Mahalwari system covered approximately 30 percent of British India.
accepted.tq: Use the middle numerical option only after distinguishing the approximate share from exact-looking distractors.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Why did the Company fix the revenue demand under the Permanent Settlement at a high level?
o: To allow the state to receive all future increases in agricultural prices.
To abolish the zamindar class immediately.
To make revenue dependent on annual crop output.
To ensure a fixed income and reduce the cost of collection.
accepted.x: The Company sought assured income and lower collection costs. However, the high fixed demand left the state without a share in later growth.
accepted.tq: Identify the administrative rationale rather than the later consequence of the settlement.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Sunset Law associated with the Permanent Settlement, an estate could be auctioned when:
o: the annual revenue was not paid by sunset on the due date
the tenant refused to accept a patta
the zamindar failed to improve the land within ten years
accepted.x: If the required revenue was not paid by sunset of the due date, the estate could be auctioned.
accepted.tq: Focus on the precise trigger for an estate sale and reject broader consequences.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The sale of many old zamindari estates under the Permanent Settlement contributed to the emergence of:
o: a new body of village karanams
a class of hereditary ryot proprietors in Madras
a new landed class of urban merchants and moneylenders
a class of Palegar intermediaries in Rayalaseema
accepted.x: Many old zamindars lost their estates for arrears, which were purchased by urban merchants and moneylenders, creating a new landed class.
accepted.tq: Trace the ownership change caused by arrears and auction sales.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which regulations empowered zamindars to seize the property of tenants under the Permanent Settlement?
accepted.x: The regulations of 1799, known as Haftam, and 1812, known as Panjam, enabled zamindars to seize tenants' property.
accepted.tq: Pair the two regulations with their coercive effect rather than with settlement dates.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following developments was associated with the Permanent Settlement?
1. Absentee landlordism
2. Sub-infeudation
3. Rack-renting
4. Reduction of peasants to tenants-at-will
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four were effects of the Permanent Settlement. The system strengthened landlordism, encouraged layers of subordinate interests and exposed peasants to insecure tenancy and high rents.
accepted.tq: Recognise a complete cluster of social and agrarian consequences.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Company's position after agricultural cultivation and prices rose after 1800:
1. The fixed demand prevented the Company from obtaining additional revenue from that growth.
2. The Company faced a dilemma because its revenue demand was not linked to rising prices.
3. The Permanent Settlement automatically increased the Company's share whenever cultivation expanded.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the fixed demand did not automatically provide the Company with additional revenue when cultivation and prices increased.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed effect of a fixed-revenue arrangement.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the Permanent Settlement, the zamindars were recognised as proprietors whose rights were generally:
o: limited to collecting taxes for one year
dependent on annual approval by village officers
accepted.x: The decennial settlement made permanent in 1793 recognised zamindars as proprietors, with rights that were alienable, rentable and heritable.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal character of proprietary rights rather than their revenue obligation.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The decennial settlement under the Permanent Settlement was made permanent in:
accepted.x: The ten-year, or decennial, settlement was made permanent in 1793.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of permanent confirmation from the years of later coercive regulations.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the commonly cited distribution of rent under the Permanent Settlement, what share was retained by the zamindar?
accepted.x: The commonly cited distribution gave the state 10/11 of the rent collected and the zamindar 1/11. Some accounts mention a 9/10 and 1/10 division, but the cited assessment here uses 1/11.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the zamindar's retained share from the much larger state share.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a rationale advanced for making the Permanent Settlement revenue demand fixed?
o: Ensuring that the Company would receive every future increase in agricultural prices
Reducing the cost of revenue collection
Securing an assured income for the Company
accepted.x: The rationale included assured income, lower collection costs, a loyal landlord class and the hope that zamindars would improve the land. A fixed demand actually prevented the Company from receiving additional revenue from later price increases.
accepted.tq: Find the option that contradicts the economic consequence of revenue fixity.
accepted.sec: Permanent Settlement - high revenue demand, Sunset Law, litigation, zamindari sales  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following developments associated with land revenue administration in chronological order:
A. Baramahal came under Company control after the Third Mysore War
B. Regulation VII of 1822 associated with Holt Mackenzie
C. Regulation IX of 1833 associated with R.M. Bird
D. Permanent Settlement made permanent
accepted.x: Baramahal came under Company control in 1792, the Permanent Settlement became permanent in 1793, Regulation VII was issued in 1822 and Regulation IX in 1833.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two nineteenth-century regulations.
accepted.sec: Mahalwari - areas and officials → role  [APPSC]
